text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: inference-prod (us-west-2a). Elevated 5xx rates and increased tail latency detected. PD# 98321. Auto-esc to oncall.

sre-oncall: I'm on page. Pulling metrics and logs now. Which rollout is active?

claudia: Latest rollout is v2.14. Health shows ~18% 502s for the service behind nlb-usw2a-inference.

matt: I can repro a 502 from the gateway: `curl -v https://gateway-usw2a.redwood.internal/health/stream` -> `502` intermittently.

pam-support: Support seeing customer error spikes for three tenants (kognify, docsprint, qa-suite). Notifying accounts.

sre-oncall: Checking DNS pathing — running a few probes to resolver and node.

claudia: `dig @10.10.5.2 inference-svc.usw2a.internal` returns NXDOMAIN ~30% of the time. Resolver rtts are spiky.

dev-ops: Network plane shows rx packet drops on host az1a-ephemeral-003 around same window. Kernel counters rising.

matt: Logs show repeated `ENETUNREACH` from proxy -> backend containers. Sample from gateway logs: ```
[2026-03-16T14:12:07Z] grpc: error transport: Error while dialing backend: dial tcp 10.2.3.45:7000: connect: network is unreachable
```

sre-oncall: Hypothesis: resolver instability causing backend connection failures and NLB health flaps. Two mitigation paths: (A) steer traffic off us-west-2a to eu-west-1 / us-east-1, or (B) try local host-level workarounds (restart nic, adjust qdisc). Which is faster?

claudia: Steering is safest short-term. I'll prepare a 30% warm-steer to eu1 and 20% to us-east. Keep 50% local to observe.

matt: Applying route change: `redwoodctl route adjust --service inference-prod --policy emergency-steer --weights us-west-2a:50,eu-west-1:30,us-east-1:20`

incident-bot: Route change applied (audit id rca-20260316-1). Traffic rebalancing starting now.

pam-support: Notified affected customers: initial comm sent. Will publish status page: "Partial degradation in us-west-2a; mitigation in progress."

sre-oncall: After steer: 502s dropped from 18% -> 6% in 3m. Latency tail improved for non-steered traffic. Good progress.

claudia: Still seeing occasional NXDOMAIN for internal resolver; filing a cloud ticket for AZ resolver instability.

dev-ops: On the ephemeral hosts we saw `qdisc` congestion. I restarted network agent on az1a-ephemeral-003 and that host's connections recovered. But there's correlated packet loss across other hosts.

matt: Suggest we keep the steer for 30m, then gradually shift back if ticket resolves. Also enable fallback model variant for small customers to reduce retries.

sre-oncall: Agreed. I'll keep monitoring; setting next update in 10m. Handing a short runbook to next oncall: note PD# 98321, audit rca-20260316-1, steer policy emergency-steer active at 30m mark.

pam-support: Updated status page and support thread with current mitigation and ETA. Customers asked for an incident update cadence: 15m.

claudia: Filing internal post-incident action: investigate resolver TTL/route flaps and kernel tx scheduling on G5 hosts in us-west-2a.

dev-ops: Opened cloud ticket with AWS referencing VPC resolver flapping and host-level packet loss. Ticket # AWS-772331.

sre-oncall: Leaving this thread to next oncall in 20m (rotation: @matt -> @claudia). If anything spikes, re-escalate. Thanks team. :white_check_mark:
